[[Huntington, West Virginia]] }} '''Patrick Patterson''' (born March 14, 1989 in [[Washington, D.C.]]{{cite web|title=USABasketball Bio: Patrick Patterson|publisher = USA Basketball, Inc.|date=2007-03-21|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/patrick_patterson_bio.html|accessdate = 2007-05-24}}) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[University of Kentucky]]. He is a 6'8", 235 lb. [[McDonald's All-American]] [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]]. He grew up in [[Huntington, West Virginia]]{{cite web |title = ESPN Recruit Tracker: Patrick Patterson |publisher = ESPN |date = 2007-05-16 |url = http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player?recruitId=43944&season=2007&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fplayer%3frecruitId%3d43944%26season%3d2007 |accessdate = 2007-05-24 }}, and helped lead [[Huntington High School (West Virginia)|Huntington High School]] to three-straight state championships, the last one with help from [[O. J. Mayo]]. ==Collegiate Career== Patrick Patterson played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Kentucky]]. He chose to play for Kentucky rather than [[Duke University|Duke]] or [[University of Florida|Florida]] in a highly publicized recruiting battle. He was recruited by Kentucky Coach [[Tubby Smith]] and his replacement [[Billy Gillispie]].{{cite web |title = Patterson's choice a surprise to the end |publisher = ''The Herald-Dispatch'' |date = 2007-05-18 |url = http://www.herald-dispatch.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070518/SPORTS02/705180358/1014 |accessdate = 2007-05-24 }} {{cite web|url=http://kentucky.scout.com/a.z?s=48&p=9&c=8&cfg=bb&yr=2007|title=Basketball Recruiting: Kentucky|date=2007|work=Scout.com.|publisher=Scout.com.|accessdate=2009-04-11}} In the 2009-2010 season he is playing for former Memphis coach [[John Calipari]] who became Billy Gillispie's replacement in April 2009. ===Freshman Season=== During Patterson's freshman All-American 2007-2008 season, Patterson averaged 16.4 [[point (basketball)|point]]s, 7.7 [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s, 1.2 [[block (basketball)|block]]s, 0.8 [[steal (basketball)|steal]]s, while shooting 57% from the [[field goal (basketball)|field]]. After a Kentucky victory over the [[Ole Miss Rebels]], Patterson missed the remainder of the 2007-2008 season with a [[stress fracture]] in his left ankle. He also claimed he planned on staying at Kentucky rather than participating in the [[NBA Draft]]. ===Sophomore Season=== For his [[sophomore]] season at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|UK]] during the 2008-09 season, he and fellow teammate [[Jodie Meeks]] became one of the most successful duos that season, and also became the most productive duo at Kentucky, since the days of [[Dan Issel]] and [[Mike Pratt (basketball)|Mike Pratt]]. Patterson scored a career high 33 points on December 22, 2008 against the [[Tennessee State University|Tennessee State Tigers]]. During Patterson's sophomore 2008-2009 season, he averaged 17.9 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.1 blocks, 0.6 steals, while shooting 60% from the field. April 18, 2009, Patterson decided to enter his name into the [[2009 NBA Draft]]. However, Patrick decided he would return to Kentucky for a third season on May 8th, 2009. ===Junior Season=== Patterson continued to play a crucial role for the team during his junior season. However, with the addition of freshman players [[John Wall (basketball)|John Wall]], [[DeMarcus Cousins]], and [[Eric Bledsoe]], Patterson was no longer required to be the main option for scoring and rebounding. Patterson also improved his outside shot, shooting about 40% from the 3 point line all season (compared to no 3-pointers made in the previous seasons). During this season, Patterson helped the team win the [[2010 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|SEC Tournament]] and achieve a #1 seed in the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2004. On April 23, 2010, Patterson decided to forgo his senior season and declared for the [[2010 NBA Draft]].http://www.nba.com/2010/news/04/23/patterson.draft.ap/index.html ===College Stats=== '''Season Totals''' {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:right;" |- !
